title: Enforce the wall clock with pane.close: the interrupt is only a courtesy
description:
Split out of tick emk, which this could not finish honestly inside.

The wall clock sends interruptChord through agent.send_keys. An agent inside a long shell call never reads it: in the Phase 3 run a pi worker ran 26 minutes past its bound while the interrupt was re-delivered at every poll, and the run stalled 85 minutes until the reconciler's own deadline fired.

The enforcement exists in herdr: pane.close, params PaneTarget {pane_id}. The agent's pane is on the AgentInfo the executor already fetches. The work is protocol work, which is why it is its own tick:

- The client's method and result constants are pinned member-for-member against internal/herd/wirevocab/herd-vocabulary.json, with a drift test against the live server. pane.close is already in methods.members; it must be added to methods.client_used.
- Its RESULT discriminator is not obvious. pane_closed appears in the success_response schema but NOT in ResponseResult.oneOf, which is what the drift test pins, so pane.close may answer ok. Determine it against the live server (or herdr's source) rather than guessing — a wrong discriminator fails every call at runtime, and the client refuses a response it cannot match.
- herdtest's fake server needs the method, and its own vocabulary test covers the fake's member set.

Behaviour wanted: after the interrupt is delivered, allow a bounded grace (the executor's poll interval times a small constant, or a named constant), then close the pane, confirm through AgentGet that the agent is gone, and settle on that positive answer as a stop at the wall clock. Snapshot the worktree first, per tick pbb, or the stop destroys the work.

Do not skip the grace: an agent that DOES honour the interrupt should be allowed to exit cleanly and write its report, which is what happened for tick 55i.
acceptance_criteria: An agent that ignores the interrupt has its pane closed within a bounded grace after the wall clock and the attempt settles as stopped-at-wall-clock; an agent that honours the interrupt is never closed; both proven against the herdtest fake, and the client's new constants are pinned in the wire vocabulary with the drift test passing
